Earth is home to different biomes. Biomes are large areas with similar climates, plants, and animals. The tundra is the coldest biome. It is found in Arctic, alpine, and Antarctic regions. It has very little plant life, mostly small shrubs and mosses. This is because the ground is frozen most of the year. Closer to the equator, temperate forests have trees that lose their leaves in winter. Grasslands, like the African savanna, have mostly grasses and scattered trees. The warmest biomes are near the equator. Tropical rainforests are hot and wet all year round. They have tall trees that form a canopy that blocks sunlight from reaching the forest floor. These forests are very diverse. They are home to millions of plant and animal species like orchids, cacao trees, colorful parrots, monkeys, and jaguars. Deserts are very dry biomes. Despite the lack of water, they support plants and animals that have adapted to survive the harsh conditions.
